title: Tzatziki
subtitle: Greek yoghurt dip with cucumber, garlic, dill, and mint
excerpt: Tzatziki is a Greek condiment eaten with everything from grilled meat to flatbreads. The key is squeezing every drop of water from the grated cucumber so the dip stays thick.
sourceNotes: Tzatziki is ubiquitous across Greece and Turkey (where it is called cacik). It is part of the broader meze tradition of the Eastern Mediterranean.

recipe.batchNotes: Doubles easily. Keeps in the fridge for 3 days.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 24 hours ahead. The garlic flavour intensifies overnight.

content.text: Grate the cucumber on the coarse side of a box grater. Then squeeze it in a clean cloth or your hands until no more liquid comes out. Do not skip this step.

items.prepNote: coarsely grated and squeezed very dry

content.text: Grate the cucumber coarsely. Place in a sieve set over a bowl, sprinkle with a pinch of salt, and leave for 5 minutes. Then squeeze with your hands until very dry.
Combine the yoghurt, squeezed cucumber, garlic, olive oil, and lemon juice in a bowl.
Fold in the dill and mint. Season with salt and pepper.
Taste and adjust: it should be bright with lemon, garlicky, and well seasoned.
Spoon into a bowl. Drizzle with extra olive oil and serve cold.

items.cause: The cucumber was not squeezed dry enough.
items.fix: Tip through the sieve again and press hard to extract more liquid.

items.symptom: The garlic flavour is too sharp.
items.cause: Raw garlic can be very strong.
items.fix: Use only 1 clove next time, or grate and rest in lemon juice for 5 minutes first.
Add more lemon juice and taste again before adjusting salt.
